What You'll Be Doing

The Venture Banking Credit Analyst will be an integral part of origination, underwriting, and portfolio management. This position will be responsible for banking and lending directly to private investment funds across several asset classes. The Credit Analyst will have exposure to many different business units while creating a differentiated market strategy. This position is a full-time, regular opportunity with an anticipated start date in Summer 2027.

- Collect and review diligence materials to prepare credit memorandums for presentation to the leadership team.

- Minimum Required: Bachelor's Degree in finance, accounting or another business related field.

Regular | Full Time

Why Stifel

Stifel’s Capital Structure Advisory group has over two decades of experience guiding companies, creditors, shareholders, and sponsors through complex financial restructurings, recapitalizations, and strategic transactions. With a track record of over 190 company representations, $450 billion in restructured debt, and $21 billion in M&A advisory, Stifel CSA is known for its intellectual rigor, creativity, and hands-on approach.  Our professionals collaborate closely with Stifel’s industry bankers to provide clients access to the full spectrum of strategic alternatives. Most engagements are completed out-of-court and often remain confidential, underscoring our reputation for discretion and excellence.

Stifel CSA has a long track record with:
- Renegotiating credit facilities
- Obtaining covenant waivers and amendments
- Consummating exchange offers, tender offers and consent solicitations
- Raising capital (bank loans, second lien, DIP financings, high yield, mezzanine loans, private equity and strategic investments)
- Selling non-core assets or entire companies
- Effectuating cross border and international restructurings
- Providing expert valuation and related testimony
- Liability management transactions
- Pre-packaged / pre-arranged chapter 11 cases
- Traditional restructurings under chapter 11

Past and current clients include: GNC, Carbon Health, Del Monte creditors, Commonwealth of Puerto Rico creditors, Yellow Corp. creditors, Lazydays, Checkers Restaurants, MOD Super Fast Pizza, CorEnergy Infrastructure Trust, Invacare, Rockport, Structurlam, Nice-Pak Products, Workhorse, Mallinckrodt creditors, Sequential Brands Group, TNT Crane & Rigging and Faraday Future.

What You'll Be Doing

Senior Analysts / Junior Associates will contribute meaningfully to active engagements and internal initiatives.

What We're Looking For

Senior Analysts / Junior Associates will contribute meaningfully to active engagements and internal initiatives. Responsibilities include:
- Preparing presentation materials such as pitchbooks and summaries
- Conducting in-depth industry and company research
- Building and analyzing financial models to evaluate company projections and strategic alternatives
- Supporting the development of industry databases and valuation analyses
- Analyze credit agreements, indentures, and covenant compliance
- Working closely with deal teams, including other junior and senior bankers

What You'll Bring

We seek candidates with strong academic performance, demonstrated leadership, and a passion for finance and restructuring. Ideal candidates will possess:
- Exceptional quantitative and analytical skills
- Superior attention to detail and disciplined work ethic
- Strong verbal and written communication abilities
- Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment
- Proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint
- Financial modeling and/or accounting experience
- Collaborative mindset and strong interpersonal skills

Education & Experience

- Minimum Required: Bachelor's degree in Finance or related field
- Minimum Required: 1-4 years  experience in corporate restructuring, investment banking or similar field

Licenses & Credentials

- Minimum Required: None

Systems & Technology

- Minimum Required: None

Compensation Range

Salary: USD $125,000.00/Yr. - USD $200,000.00/Yr.

Actual salaries may vary, and may be based on several factors, including but not limited to each candidate’s qualifications, skills, and overall competencies for the position. The base salary is one component of Stifel’s overall compensation package for each individual employee. Other benefits and offerings include, but not limited to, discretionary bonuses, health / dental / vision / prescription insurance offerings, Stifel Total Health Connect, flexible spending accounts, tuition & certification assistance programs, paid time off, and much, much more! To view a more comprehensive list of Stifel’s current offerings, please visit https://www.stifel.com/careers/benefits. Applications are accepted until the position is filled.

About Stifel

At its core, the Stifel story is a journey of growth and optimism for the future. In our more than 125-year history, Stifel has evolved from a St. Louis-based brokerage house and is now a full-service investment bank, offering securities brokerage, trading, research, underwriting and corporate advisory services globally.  Our expertise spans sectors and products in both public and private markets. We are driven by relationships, not transactions, and are committed to earning long-term trust from our clients.

Our investment banking division provides a broad range of industry-leading services to its clients, including merger and acquisition advisory services, debt and equity financings, balance sheet restructuring, and mutual thrift & insurance company conversions.  The combination of a full-service product offering and more than 600 bankers’ deep domain and product expertise allows us to provide solutions that meet the evolving needs of our clients.

Stifel’s success is rooted in the power of our people and platform. We provide our employees an entrepreneurial environment that rewards collaboration and hard work.  We are looking to engage with and hire talented candidates from all backgrounds – specifically, those who have the desire to expand their skills and realize ambitious goals. We are committed to a workplace that reflects the clients we serve and the communities where we live and work.

The Fund Banking group consists of 10+ people and manages a portfolio of $8B+ in credit commitments spanning across 300+ investment firm client relationships. The Fund Banking group works closely with other investor-facing business units within Stifel such as Stifel Venture Banking with works directly with portfolio companies of venture capital funds.

This Director/Managing Director position will be the lead business development position for New York City and surrounding northeast geographies. In this role, you will be focused on building new Fund Banking / Fund Finance business with VC/PE firms and being the senior relationship manager to those firms.

What We're Looking For

- Originate, develop, and maintain Fund Banking / Fund Finance business independently, primarily out of New York City.
- Develop and maintain a network of venture capital and private equity firms. A high level of business development activity and relationship building will be expected. Strong presence in New York City is required.
- Negotiate and structure Fund Banking / Fund Finance credit facilities from the ground up. Most facilities will be bilateral capital call (subscription) credit facilities with credit situational facilities to management companies and general partners.
- Partner and cross-sell with peer departments at Stifel (Venture Banking, Investment Banking, Commercial Lending, Fixed Income, and Private Client) to identify and generate opportunities.
- Assist in the management and coaching of new Fund Banking team members.
- Partner with Stifel portfolio managers, analysts and risk management to proactively manage and maintain desired credit quality. Strong underwriting and deal structuring skills are critical.
- Maintain in-depth knowledge of the VC/PE and Fund Finance ecosystems along with Stifel’s broad offering of products

What You'll Bring

- Direct experience in a business development role engaging with VC/PE funds
- Knowledge of structuring and managing Fund Finance credit facilities
- Knowledge of treasury management and depository needs of VC/PE firms and their fund administrators
- Exposure and pre-existing relationships within the VC/PE ecosystem
- Effective communication skills to properly interact with prospective clients, including senior partners at VC/PE firms
- Experience managing effective teams. Strong team leadership skills with experience recruiting, coaching and developing talent pipeline
- Outgoing and confident personality with the ability to attend many in-person industry events within the VC/PE ecosystem ecosystem

The role is responsible for supporting and enhancing the commercial compliance program through risk assessments, monitoring and testing, regulatory change management, issue oversight, and governance reporting. The Commercial Banking Compliance Officer provides compliance guidance and credible challenge to business partners and helps ensure adherence to applicable laws, regulations, supervisory expectations, and internal policies. This position works closely with commercial lending, Fund Banking, Venture Banking, BSA/AML, OFAC, Legal, Risk Management, and Internal Audit to identify and mitigate compliance risks while promoting strong governance and safe and sound banking practices.

What We're Looking For

- Develop, maintain, and enhance a risk-based Commercial Banking Compliance framework aligned with the Bank's commercial activities, products, and growth strategy.
- Perform independent compliance monitoring and testing to evaluate adherence to applicable laws, regulations, Bank policies, and procedures.
- Conduct commercial compliance risk assessments by identifying risks, evaluating controls, documenting results, and recommending enhancements.
- Provide second-line oversight and credible challenge for commercial lending compliance requirements, including Flood Insurance, Regulation B/ECOA, FCRA, fair lending, and related documentation controls.
- Provide compliance guidance and oversight for Fund Banking, Venture Banking, subscription facilities, capital call lending, complex ownership structures, and other specialized commercial lending activities.
- Evaluate compliance risks associated with foreign investors, offshore fund structures, beneficial ownership complexity, international affiliations, and cross-border relationships.
- Assess regulatory changes, new products, and business initiatives to identify compliance impacts and recommend updates to controls, procedures, training, and reporting.
- Manage and support issue remediation activities by identifying root causes, validating corrective actions, tracking progress, and escalating material concerns.
- Prepare and deliver compliance reporting, monitoring results, dashboards, regulatory analyses, and governance materials for management, committees, audits, and regulatory examinations.
- Coordinate with BSA/AML, OFAC, Legal, Internal Audit, Credit Risk Review, Operations, and business stakeholders to support effective compliance risk management.
- Provide compliance guidance, training, and regulatory interpretation to business partners while maintaining independent second-line oversight.
- Maintain expertise in commercial banking regulations, supervisory expectations, and industry practices, and participate in strategic initiatives to identify compliance risks and control considerations.

What You'll Bring

- Working knowledge of commercial banking compliance requirements and second-line compliance risk management practices.
- Ability to interpret regulatory requirements, identify compliance risks, evaluate controls, and recommend practical risk mitigation strategies.
- Experience conducting compliance monitoring, testing, risk assessments, issue management, regulatory change management, or related compliance oversight activities.
- Knowledge of commercial lending compliance requirements, including Flood Insurance, Regulation B/ECOA, FCRA, fair lending, and related regulatory expectations.
- Experience supporting or overseeing commercial lending, Fund Banking, Venture Banking, specialized lending products, or complex commercial customer relationships preferred.
- Ability to provide independent, effective challenge while maintaining productive relationships with business partners and stakeholders.
- Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills with attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex regulatory concepts to diverse audiences.
- Ability to collaborate effectively with Legal, BSA/AML, OFAC, Risk Management, Internal Audit, Credit Risk Review, Operations, and business leaders.
- Demonstrated sound judgment, integrity, and commitment to fostering a strong culture of compliance, governance, and risk management.

Education & Experience

- Minimum Required: Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Accounting, Risk Management, Law, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
- Minimum Required: 5+ years of experience in bank compliance, commercial lending compliance, regulatory risk management, audit, credit risk, or a related banking control function.
- Preferred: Experience with specialized commercial lending activities and complex customer structures, including Fund Banking, Venture Banking, foreign investor considerations, regulatory examinations, audit support, issue remediation, or corrective action validation.

Licenses & Credentials

- Preferred: CRCM certification or progress toward certification.
- Other relevant banking, risk, audit, or compliance certifications may be considered.

Systems & Technology

- Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook, SharePoint, and Teams.
- Experience with compliance systems, risk platforms, issue management tools, or reporting dashboards preferred.
